docRequirement: memory.md:384 — "The first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation. Content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start." The cap is a MIN of two limits (200 lines AND 25KB), it applies to the loaded body, and memory.md:390 scopes it: "This limit applies only to `MEMORY.md`. CLAUDE.md files are loaded in full regardless of length" — so instruction files and rule files must stay uncapped.
current: Only the line half exists, and only on a path the shipped app never takes. `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8) is consumed by `readMemoryFile` (memory-store.ts:29-33), which is a pure line slice — `readFileSync(filePath,'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)` — with no byte check. `readMemoryFile` has exactly two non-test consumers: `readMemoryFileWithImports` (memory-store.ts:66-110) feeding the legacy composer `loadMemoryPromptBlock` (memory-store.ts:317-334), and the `@import` scan at packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:427. The legacy composer is dead on the live route: packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:453-455 is `const memoryContext = capabilityContextPinned ? '' : loadMemoryPromptBlock(...)`, and `capabilityContextPinned` (positional arg 12, system.ts:412) is passed as `this.capabilityTurnRuntime !== null` by both live backends (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6607, packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1256). The live route reads every memory layer WHOLE: packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:976-977 iterates `runtime.view.memory` calling `runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource)`, whose native branch is `const content = readFileSync(contentPath)` returned verbatim at packages/shared/src/capabilities/materializer.ts:181-186 with no cap, and base-agent.ts:1003-1014 pushes that body (only `@import` lines filtered out) into the pinned `<capability-layer>` block. The Pi projection does the same independently: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/context-resource.ts:66-68 loops `input.view.memory` and calls `addPinned('memory', ...)`, which reads via the same uncapped `materializer.readText` (context-resource.ts:51). The memory layers concerned are the real MEMORY.md files — user/global (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:909-916), session (native-sources.ts:977-986) and project — all emitted by `memoryFileRecords` (native-sources.ts:369-435). No 25KB constant exists anywhere on this path; the repo's only instruction byte cap is `MAX_NESTED_INSTRUCTION_FILE_BYTES = 10 * 1024` (native-sources.ts:772, truncation at :875-877), which governs lazily discovered nested AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instruction files — a sibling subsystem that never sees a MEMORY.md memory layer.
divergence: Two deltas, not one. (1) The 25KB byte limit does not exist at all — no constant, no check, on any path. (2) The 200-line limit exists with the right value but is wired to the wrong consumer: it caps `readMemoryFile`, which on a shipped build only serves the legacy fallback composer and the `@import` scan, while the route every turn actually takes (`composePinnedCapabilityContext` -> `materializer.readText`, and the Pi `materializePiContextResources` twin) reads MEMORY.md whole. So the observable behaviour is 'no truncation of MEMORY.md at all', even though the constant matching the doc is already in the tree. The scope carve-out at memory.md:390 is already satisfied by accident — nothing is capped, so nothing over-caps CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md or `.agents/rules` files; the fix must keep it that way rather than capping every `view.memory` layer.

change.what: Add `export const MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE_LIMIT = 25 * 1024;` next to `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT` (:8) and one exported helper `applyMemoryIndexLoadLimits(content: string): string` that walks lines accumulating `Buffer.byteLength(line, 'utf-8') + 1`, stopping at whichever of 200 lines or 25 KB comes first and dropping the line that would cross the byte budget (line-boundary cut, so no multi-byte character is split). Do NOT change `readMemoryFile` itself — native-sources.ts:427 uses it for the `@import` scan and a byte cut there would silently change which imports are discovered. Instead give `readMemoryFileWithImports` (:66) an `applyIndexLimits` flag that runs the helper on the ROOT file body (before import expansion, so imported topic files are not counted against the index's budget) and pass it true from the three MEMORY.md reads in `loadMemoryPromptBlock` (:326, :329, :330) and false for `loadUnscopedRuleMemories` (:295).

In the `runtime.view.memory` loop (:976-1014), after `const content = await runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource)` (:977), apply the cap only to the memory index: `const capped = layer.format !== 'rule' && basename(layer.resource.absolutePath) === MEMORY_FILE_NAME ? applyMemoryIndexLoadLimits(content) : content;` and use `capped` for both the `unscopedRuleBody`/body branch at :997 and the import-strip at :1003. Add `MEMORY_FILE_NAME` and `applyMemoryIndexLoadLimits` to the existing `./memory/memory-store.ts` import at :25 and `basename` to the node:path import. Roughly a three-line change plus imports.

Same cap on the Pi projection: the `for (const memory of input.view.memory)` loop (:66-68) must pass the capped body, not the raw read. Either compute `const content = applyMemoryIndexLoadLimits(await input.materializer.readText(memory.resource))` for MEMORY.md layers and hand it to `addPinned` through its existing `providedContent` parameter (:49), or share one helper with base-agent. Leaving this site uncapped means the host's pinned block and the Pi subprocess's context resource carry different bodies for the same file, and the descriptor `sha256`/`id` would no longer match the block the model sees.

That test calls `readMemoryFile` directly, i.e. the path that is dead on a live turn — keep it, but add two cases for the new helper: a 250-line file of short lines truncating at line 200, and a 50-line file of long lines truncating at the last whole line under 25 KB (proving byte-first wins when it comes first). Add one case proving a rule file read via `loadUnscopedRuleMemories` is NOT byte-capped.

The existing fixtures already build `memory: [...]` layers with `format: 'rule'` and plain variants. Add one MEMORY.md layer whose file is over both limits and assert the emitted `<capability-layer>` body stops at the limit; add a sibling assertion that a `format: 'rule'` layer and a `promptLayers` instruction layer of the same size are still emitted in full (memory.md:390).

blastRadius: Three consumers read `view.memory` bodies and two of them cross a boundary. (1) `composePinnedCapabilityContext` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:960-1072) fills `pinnedCapabilityContextCache`, which is composed once per capability generation and re-injected after compaction — so a truncation changes the pinned block on both the Claude and Pi backends. Its `emitInstructionsLoaded` payload (:1043) carries file paths only, so the hook contract is unaffected. (2) `materializePiContextResources` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/context-resource.ts:36-97) hashes the body into `PiContextResourceDescriptor.sha256`, `id` and `provenance` and ships it into the Pi subprocess — a WIRE boundary; those same descriptor strings are persisted as `resourceRefs` in the compaction continuation envelope built at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:12095-12099, so this also crosses a PERSISTENCE boundary and is a risk trigger under this repo's policy (an oversized MEMORY.md gets new descriptor ids after the fix; sessions carrying the old refs must degrade, not throw). `capabilityRefs` at SessionManager.ts:12090 uses keys plus generation only and is unaffected. (3) `harness-manifest.ts:368` folds memory layers into the manifest by handle, not body. Also touched: the legacy composer chain `prompts/system.ts:453-455` -> `loadMemoryPromptBlock`, and `capabilities/native-sources.ts:427`, which must keep the current uncapped-bytes `readMemoryFile` behaviour or the `@import` discovery set changes. Tests that build memory layers: packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/base-agent.test.ts, instructions-loaded.test.ts, nested-instruction-traversal.test.ts, packages/shared/src/agent/memory/__tests__/memory-store.test.ts, packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/safe-mode-capability-gate.test.ts:158.
userImpact: No error and nothing missing — the failure is silent context spend. A user whose MEMORY.md has grown (the fork's own `remember` tool appends to it every time the agent saves something, and the scheduled cleanup only ages out marked entries below a 256 KB ceiling — packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-cleanup.ts:33) gets the ENTIRE file re-sent inside the pinned `<capability-layer>` block on every send, on both the Pi and Claude backends. At the doc's threshold that is 25 KB the user expected to be dropped; at a few thousand lines it is hundreds of KB of every request, which on a small-context gateway model (the default `tgpt/qwen35-397b-a17b-fp8` path) shortens usable conversation and can push a turn into a context-length error whose cause is invisible from the UI — the Memory surface shows the file, not what fraction of it loads. It also inverts the doc's advice loop: a user who trims MEMORY.md 'because only the first 200 lines load' sees no change, and a user who lets it grow is never told (the write-side warning is a separate finding, f103).
notes: Every file cited was read in full at the cited ranges: memory-store.ts (constants, readMemoryFile, readMemoryFileWithImports, loadUnscopedRuleMemories, loadMemoryPromptBlock), base-agent.ts:957-1072, capabilities/materializer.ts:140-209, prompts/system.ts:400-460, capabilities/native-sources.ts:360-435 and 895-990 plus its byte-cap constants, pi-harness/context-resource.ts:1-97, capabilities/resolver.ts:561-572 (RuntimeMemoryHandle: `format?: 'rule'`, `importParentPath?`), views.ts:110-165, memory-store.test.ts:35-59, SessionManager.ts:12075-12100. Absence of a 25KB cap checked with `grep -rna` (NUL-safe) for `25 * 1024` / `25600` / `25_000` across packages and apps — the only hits are unrelated token thresholds. Sequencing caveat: memory.md:386-388 says the measurement counts only the content that loads, because "YAML frontmatter and block-level HTML comments are stripped before the index is loaded" — that stripping is finding f101 and the write-side over-limit error is f103. Whichever lands second must reuse the same helper, or the load cap and the write-side check will measure different byte counts. Not verified by running the app: I did not execute a packaged build to observe an oversized MEMORY.md in a live prompt; the live-path conclusion rests on the `capabilityContextPinned` wiring read at pi-agent.ts:6607 / claude-agent.ts:1256. One scope judgement is mine, not the doc's: the fork also treats `.agents/rules` and `.claude/rules` files as `view.memory` layers, and memory.md:390 caps only MEMORY.md, so the fix keys on the file's basename rather than on the layer kind.
